senses.definition: A worker who checks parts of a building project against rules for that work.
senses.example: The building inspector visited while the pipes were still visible.

senses.definition: A person who plans or looks after structures and systems such as roads, bridges, and water networks.
senses.example: A civil engineer studied several places where a new bridge might cross the river.

senses.definition: A worker who makes careful measurements of positions, heights, or boundaries on land.
senses.example: A land surveyor measured the location of the hill before the new path was drawn.

senses.definition: A person who checks that parts or products match their planned size, shape, or other requirements.
senses.example: The quality control inspector measured a metal part before the factory shipped it.

senses.definition: A person who collects or delivers mail along an assigned route.
senses.example: The letter carrier stopped at the houses on our street.

senses.definition: The address on a piece of mail showing where it came from, so it can go back if needed.
senses.example: The return address was in the top left corner of the envelope.

senses.definition: A set of numbers in a United States address that helps direct mail toward the right delivery area.
senses.example: Two houses on the same block can share a ZIP Code.

senses.definition: A label on a piece of mail showing that some or all of the cost of sending it has been paid.
senses.example: The postage stamp on the envelope showed a picture of a bird.

senses.definition: A large pipe in a network that carries water toward many places that need it.
senses.example: The water main under the street supplies several buildings.

senses.definition: A sewer pipe that carries water pushed along by a pump, rather than depending only on gravity.
senses.example: A pump moved the water into a force main so it could reach higher ground.

senses.definition: A device that measures the amount of water passing through a pipe.
senses.example: Comparing two water meter readings showed how much water the building had used.

senses.definition: A device that measures the electrical energy that passes into a place such as a building.
senses.example: The electricity meter kept counting while the lights and computers were on.

senses.definition: A unit for an amount of electrical energy equal to one kilowatt of power used for one hour.
senses.example: The bill showed how many kilowatt-hours the building had used.

senses.definition: Workers who help service an airplane or handle its loads while it is on the ground.
senses.example: A ground crew moved suitcases between the plane and the airport building.

senses.definition: A place where collection trucks unload waste so it can be put onto larger vehicles for another trip.
senses.example: The neighborhood truck unloaded at a waste transfer station.

senses.definition: A place that gathers products before sending the right amounts on to different destinations.
senses.example: The distribution center sent one load to three small shops.

senses.definition: A series of cold places and cooled trips that keep goods cold as they travel.
senses.example: The delivery company used a cold chain to keep the ice cream frozen.

senses.definition: A train built to carry goods such as boxes, building materials, or grain.
senses.example: The freight train carried containers from the port toward several cities.
